### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and best results. | # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips | |---|------------|----------------|------| | 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.) | List components, compare prices, set a realistic budget. | | 2 | **Gather Tools & Workspace** | Clean, static‑free area | 1. Anti‑static wrist strap (recommended). 2. Phillips screwdriver. 3. Small flathead screwdriver. 4. Cable ties. 5. Work surface with good lighting. | | 3 | **Choose Components** | Compatibility is key | • CPU + Motherboard (socket match).
• RAM (speed, capacity).
• GPU (if not integrated).
• Storage (SSD/HDD).
• PSU (wattage + 80+ rating).
• Case (size, airflow).
• Cooling (stock or aftermarket). | | 4 | **Read Manuals** | Avoid mistakes | Keep motherboard, case, PSU manuals handy. | | 5 | **Prepare the Case** | Easier installation | Remove side panels, lay case flat. | | 6 | **Install the Power Supply** | Power is the backbone | • Align PSU with rear exhaust.
• Secure with screws.
• Route cables to the back. | | 7 | **Mount the Motherboard** | Foundation | • Install standoffs in the case matching motherboard holes.
• Align with I/O shield.
• Screw down lightly. | | 8 | **Install the CPU** | Core of performance | • Open CPU socket latch.
• Align pin/land pattern.
• Gently place CPU.
• Lock latch. | | 9 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install Cooler** | Heat dissipation | • Use a pea‑size amount of paste.
• Place cooler, secure screws.
• Connect fan header. | | 10 | **Insert RAM** | Memory slots | • Open slot latches.
• Align notch.
• Push until clicks. | | 11 | **Mount Storage Drives** | SSD/HDD bays | • Slide into 2.5” or 3.5” bays.
• Secure screws.
• Connect SATA + power cables. | | 12 | **Install GPU (if applicable)** | Graphics power | • Remove PCIe slot covers.
• Insert card, lock latch.
• Connect 6/8‑pin power. | | 13 | **Connect Front Panel & USB** | Basic functionality | • Refer to motherboard manual for pin layout.
• Connect power button, reset, USB, audio jacks. | | 14 | **Cable Management** | Airflow & aesthetics | • Route cables neatly.
• Use cable ties or Velcro straps.
• Keep airflow paths clear. | | 15 | **Double‑Check Connections** | Prevent boot failures | • Ensure all power connectors are seated.
• Verify no loose screws or cables. | | 16 | **Power On & BIOS Setup** | First boot | • Connect monitor, keyboard, mouse.
• Press power button.
• Enter BIOS (usually DEL/F2).
• Check CPU, RAM, storage detection.
• Set boot priority to USB/SSD. | | 17 | **Install Operating System** | System ready | • Create bootable USB (Windows, Linux).
• Boot from USB, follow installer.
• Install drivers (chipset, GPU). | | 18 | **Update Firmware & Drivers** | Stability & performance | • Update BIOS if needed.
• Install latest GPU drivers.
• Install motherboard chipset drivers. | | 19 | **Run Benchmarks & Stress Tests** | Verify stability | • Use 3DMark, Cinebench, Prime95, MemTest86.
• Monitor temperatures. | | 20 | **Enjoy & Maintain** | Longevity | • Keep case dust‑free.
• Update drivers regularly.
• Monitor temperatures. | --- #### Quick Component Checklist | Category | Typical Choices (2026) | Notes | |----------|------------------------|-------| | **CPU** | AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D, Intel Core i7‑14700K | Balance of price/performance | | **Motherboard** | B650 / Z790 | Ensure BIOS supports chosen CPU | | **RAM** | 32 GB DDR5‑6000 | Future‑proof, gaming & content creation | | **GPU** | RTX 4080 / RTX 4090 | Depends on budget & resolution | | **Storage** | 1 TB NVMe SSD (PCIe 4.0) | Fast boot & load times | | **PSU** | 750 W 80+ Gold | Sufficient headroom | | **Case** | Mid‑tower ATX, good airflow | 120 mm fans, cable management | | **Cooling** | 240 mm AIO or high‑end air cooler | Keep temps < 70 °C under load | --- #### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **Short circuits** | Use anti‑static wrist strap; avoid touching metal contacts. | | **CPU not detected** | Check socket alignment; ensure BIOS updated. | | **GPU not recognized** | Verify power connectors; check BIOS for PCIe settings. | | **No POST** | Double‑check power cables; remove all peripherals except essential ones. | | **High temperatures** | Improve cable routing; add case fans; consider better cooler. | --- #### Final Thought Building a PC is as rewarding as it is practical. Take your time, double‑check each step, and enjoy the process of creating a machine tailored to your needs. Happy building!
